item.title: Zaporizhzhia airstrikes kill 17 as Russia intensifies attacks across Ukraine
item.description: Zaporizhzhia was hit by deadly Russian airstrikes on Saturday, 10 October, killing at least 17 people, including three children, Ukrainian officials said. Rescuers searched rubble for survivors as the city faced renewed strikes on residential areas.

item.title: ‘It’s a constant race’: the volunteers protecting Kyiv’s skies from new jet-powered drones
item.description:
Russia’s latest weapons have left Ukraine’s civilian air defence teams frantically trying to adapt as winter approaches

Several hours into Kyiv’s nightly curfew, much of the capital lay dark and quiet. High above, on the roof of a grey tower block on the city’s outskirts, a small group of men in uniform stood beside two heavy machine guns, scanning the horizon. Soon, a drone appeared.

Once, its unmistakable buzz would have sent the men scrambling towards their weapons. Now, the air defence unit will check speed and altitude on a monitor before taking a decision.

The Mriya air defence crew on a rooftop in Kyiv.

item.title: Britain stands behind Zelenskyy, says Streeting after Trump’s call for new leader in Ukraine
item.description:
Defence secretary backs Ukrainian president and says priority is to maintain western unity over Russia conflict

Britain stands behind Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the defence secretary has said, after Donald Trump called for the Ukrainian president to be replaced and the US announced a controversial agreement to buy Russian diesel.

Wes Streeting said Ukrainians alone should be able to decide who leads their country as he indicated Trump was facing domestic political pressure over fuel prices before next month’s midterm elections.

item.title: Former Irish Olympic swimming coach and child abuser George Gibney to be sentenced
item.description:
Gibney, 77, will face justice for abusing athletes in the 1970s and 80s after decades of effort to track and extradite him

More than half a century after he started sexually abusing children, and enjoyed prestige as Ireland’s Olympic swimming coach before fleeing to the United States, George Gibney is to face justice.

The 77-year-old will be sentenced at the central criminal court in Dublin on Monday for abusing four young female athletes in the 1970s and 1980s.

item.title: ‘Stab to the heart’: arrest of German ex-spymaster sparks calls for reform
item.description:
Claims that August Hanning exploited intelligence for private clients comes after other troubling espionage scandals

The ex-spymaster August Hanning once criticised Germany’s own intelligence services as “vegetarians” among prowling carnivores, demanding broader powers to keep the country safe in a treacherous world.

Often described as a “godfather” of Germany’s 21st-century security architecture, Hanning is now charged with treasonous espionage and handing state secrets to a foreign power in one of the most spectacular alleged intelligence breaches of the postwar period.
